ai-at-work.title: Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage
ai-at-work.excerpt: The company is said to be significantly dropping the amount it's spending on AI for its engineering teams.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Apple is pulling back spending on AI tools for its own engineers, reportedly cutting budgets that were meant to boost internal productivity. This matters because if a company with Apple's resources and AI expertise decides AI doesn't yet deliver enough ROI for their own knowledge workers, it raises hard questions about whether enterprises should be chasing these same tools right now. After thirty years in this space, I'd say this is the clearest signal yet that the AI productivity revolution is still mostly theoretical, and your CFO might be smarter to wait for proof before betting the department budget on it.

ai-at-work.title: Nothing CEO says company’s mysterious AI-first device is dropping next month
ai-at-work.excerpt: While it's not yet clear what kind of product the smartphone startup is cooking up, Nothing's CEO said the product is designed to leverage AI for productivity gains.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nothing is launching a mysterious AI device next month that the CEO claims will boost productivity, though nobody actually knows what it does yet. For digital workplace pros evaluating emerging tech, this matters because every vendor from here to Tuesday is slapping "AI-first" on whatever they're shipping, and we need to wait and see if this is genuinely useful or just another shiny thing that solves problems nobody has. After 30 years in this space, I've learned that vague productivity promises from startups usually mean either a brilliant innovation or an expensive paperweight, and the odds aren't great.

ai-at-work.title: OpenAI is already trying to shape the 2028 election
ai-at-work.excerpt: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane wants AI to define the 2028 election, proposing a new social contract that could benefit Americans while also advancing the AI giant’s own business interests.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI's chief policy officer is explicitly pitching AI as central to the 2028 election while positioning his company to benefit from that influence. This matters because digital workplace leaders are watching how AI vendors use political access to shape policy, which directly affects what tools get mandated at work and how regulation will constrain (or enable) their use. Here's the thing: when someone tells you upfront they want their product to "define" an election while advancing business interests, at least they're being honest about the conflict.

ai-at-work.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
ai-at-work.excerpt: The startup allows software engineers to deploy teams of agents to work on various aspects of a project simultaneously.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Meta just bought Conductor, an AI coding startup that lets engineers spin up teams of AI agents to work on different parts of a software project at the same time. This matters because it signals that major tech companies are betting serious money on AI agents handling actual development work, which will reshape how technical teams operate and what skills stay valuable. Honestly, if an AI agent can deploy other AI agents, we're either about to solve software bottlenecks or create a beautiful mess where nobody knows which agent broke what.

tools-tech.title: Can Netflix’s new AI tool stop your TV-streaming doomscrolling? How to try it
tools-tech.excerpt: Netflix is adding a new Discover feature, which recommends tailored streaming selections. Here’s how it works.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Netflix rolled out an AI-powered Discover feature that generates personalized streaming recommendations to help users cut through content overload. This matters to digital workplace folks because the same decision fatigue that paralyzes people choosing between five thousand shows is exactly what kills productivity when employees face infinite tool options and poorly organized knowledge systems. Here's the thing though: Netflix thinks AI recommendations will stop doomscrolling, but I've watched people spend 45 minutes reading *about* what to watch instead of actually watching anything. Same energy as implementing another collaboration tool to solve your collaboration problem.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft files patent for AI that can alter what people say during live broadcasts
tools-tech.excerpt: Microsoft has filed a patent application for a new AI technology that can alter what people say during live broadcasts. The technology is designed to automatically identify what is being said and can
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft filed a patent for AI that can edit what people say in real-time broadcasts by swapping words and syncing mouth movements to match the altered audio. This matters to digital workplace pros because deepfake technology like this will inevitably land in your organization's video conferencing, training content, and internal broadcasts, whether you want it or not. The stated use case is translation, which is fine, but we all know this tech will be weaponized for misinformation faster than you can say "trust but verify."

tools-tech.title: Apple’s Q4 results show the enterprise tide turning to local AI
tools-tech.excerpt: While delivering record Q4 revenue, Apple’s financial results revealed a $33 billion cost associated with memory price inflation, representing the true cost of the growing bubble of AI data center inv
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple's Q4 earnings revealed that enterprises are shifting toward on-device AI processing instead of relying on centralized data centers, driven by concerns about inference costs, security, and data governance. This matters because it signals that the massive cloud AI infrastructure investments everyone's been hyping might not pay off the way vendors promised, which means your organization's AI strategy needs a reality check. The irony is delicious: the same cost pressures that made cloud AI attractive are now pushing companies back toward local processing, which means you'll be managing AI deployments across devices instead of in shiny data centers.

tools-tech.title: Google’s first AI data center in space is up and running
tools-tech.excerpt: Google’s first experimental data center satellite as part of the Suncatcher project is now operational. The satellite was launched in October, and after several weeks of testing, it has begun communic
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google launched an experimental AI data center satellite called Suncatcher that's now operational, equipped with four TPUs that can generate a kilowatt of power and communicate with Earth. For digital workplace folks, this matters because it signals where computational infrastructure is heading: distributed, off-planet, and built around AI processing at scale. Look, I've seen a lot of bold moves in 30 years, but putting your AI chips in orbit feels less like innovation and more like what happens when engineers have too much budget and not enough Earth-based problems to solve first.

digital-culture.title: Four ways to manage an AI agent successfully
digital-culture.excerpt: Last month, a friend told me that by the end of the year, his startup will have seven employees and over 20 AI agents. He has led several previous successful organizations and has a reputation as a wo
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company ran a piece about managing AI agents effectively, focusing on how leaders can maintain team cohesion when AI becomes a major organizational presence. This matters because the digital workplace is shifting from "how do we adopt AI" to "how do we actually work alongside it day-to-day," and most managers have zero playbook for that. Here's the thing: if your biggest management challenge used to be Karen in accounting, you're about to learn that managing non-humans is a whole different headache, but honestly, at least they don't need PTO.

digital-culture.title: How ‘deep reading’ can cure your brain rot
digital-culture.excerpt: Everyone has something to say about the state of reading in 2026: Reading comprehension scores in the U.S. have continued to decline. Many college students cannot make it through an entire book. The m
digital-culture.dwp_take: Reading comprehension is tanking across America while Gen Z paradoxically claims a reading identity, suggesting a real gap between consuming content and actually understanding it. Digital workplace pros need to care because knowledge workers who can't focus long enough to digest complex information become liabilities in knowledge-intensive roles. Here's the uncomfortable truth: if your team can't read past a headline, they'll struggle with anything deeper than Slack messages, and that's exactly when your culture starts running on vibes instead of substance.

digital-culture.title: Canva’s restructuring affects more than 1,200 people. But its severance package is earning praise
digital-culture.excerpt: Design tech company Canva is doing some major restructuring: The move will impact nearly 1,300 employees, or roughly 22% of its staff. But the company’s also getting attention for how it’s treating th
digital-culture.dwp_take: Canva is cutting 1,300 jobs, about 22% of its workforce, but doing it with a severance package that's actually making people nod instead of rage-quit. This matters because most tech layoffs treat departing employees like they've already left the building, so when a company handles it decently, it signals something about workplace culture that the rest of us are watching. The real test isn't the initial announcement though, it's whether those laid-off folks actually receive what was promised and whether Canva's remaining team stays motivated or just starts updating their LinkedIn profiles out of habit.

digital-culture.title: How AI impacts solopreneurs’ relationships with their clients (and what to do about it)
digital-culture.excerpt: Most people I know have asked themselves some version of “Is AI replacing me?” It’s a fair question. But, running a solo business, I think the question extends beyond “Is AI replacing the work I do?”
digital-culture.dwp_take: Solopreneurs are discovering that AI isn't just replacing their work, it's changing how clients value them and expect pricing to drop accordingly. This matters because freelancers and independent operators now face a dual pressure: delivering better work faster while justifying fees that clients think AI should handle for pennies. The real problem isn't the technology, it's that clients conflating "AI can do this" with "AI can do this well" is a recipe for race-to-the-bottom pricing that nobody actually wins.

industry-news.excerpt: US voters are pushing back against AI data centers, raising concerns about construction delays, energy costs, and the future of AI infrastructure. The post AI Data Center Boom Faces Backlash After US
industry-news.dwp_take: US voters are increasingly opposing AI data center construction in their communities due to concerns about delays, energy consumption, and infrastructure strain. This matters to digital workplace pros because the backbone of every cloud service, collaboration platform, and AI tool we rely on depends on these data centers, so community resistance directly impacts where and how fast new workplace tech gets deployed. Turns out people don't want a glowing server farm in their backyard, even if it powers their Slack messages—who knew?

industry-news.dwp_take: Android 17 is rolling out across major phone brands with varying timelines and eligibility requirements depending on your device. This matters because your workforce is almost certainly fragmented across these devices, and OS updates create security patches, compatibility issues, and support headaches that IT has to manage. After 30 years watching mobile updates wreak havoc on enterprise deployments, my advice is simple: don't let your team update until your IT team says it's safe, no matter how shiny Android 17 looks.

industry-news.dwp_take: Organizations are scrambling to figure out who actually owns AI agent access and who gets blamed when things go sideways. The real talk is that most companies are still playing governance theater while their AI agents are out there making decisions like they own the place, so get your audit trails and shutdown buttons ready before your CEO learns about it from the news.
